status: Uniform compact-family Sobolev gains and a compact stronger Miura lift cover proved; finite-p potential image and endpoint conclusion remain open
results: A compact compatible family of actual real sources and weighted realizations has one cutoff controlling both signed canonical center-gap estimates, every larger remainder cutoff and the full physical Fourier-tail recurrence.
Compact maxima and Dini convergence give one vanishing Fourier-tail envelope. Its forced quadratic recurrence preserves the common actual-gap forcing and transfers summability on geometric scales.

A quantitative geometric-shell estimate bounds the entire Sobolev norm, including the finite head, by the common weighted geometric-tail budget. Both original source components gain one uniform stronger norm bound at the exact remainder threshold.

Vanishing Fourier multipliers turn uniformly norm-bounded coefficientwise continuous families into norm-continuous families. This yields exact Sobolev realizations at every strictly lower order, with compact range on compact parameter spaces.
Even physical sampling yields the exact unit-period Sobolev weight with a contractive full-norm estimate. The original Fourier convention and both signed frequencies are retained.

Finite iteration yields a continuous compact realization at every nonnegative s strictly below a common actual-gap majorant order S, for every finite p>1. Each step uses a gain whose p-power lies below min(1,p-1) and spends part of that gain to retain compactness.

All real scalar lifts in ONE ACTUAL Hilbert Dirac isospectral set have the same canonically indexed gaps. Gap regularity at S therefore gives a compact scalar Sobolev realization at every nonnegative s<S, with original raw unit-period coefficients retained.

For the ENTIRE original H-minus-one Hill isospectral set, actual original gaps at order -a give one common physical shift and one compact Sobolev lift cover at every order 1-b with a<b<=1 and finite p>=2. Every original isospectral member is exactly the shifted rough Miura image of a member of that cover.
qualifications: General compact-family theorems require continuous original real-source and weighted realizations on a compact nonempty parameter space. A common gap majorant is a proved hypothesis, not inferred from separate pointwise bounds.
All algebraic remainder thresholds retain s*p.toReal<min(1,p.toReal-1). The gain is positive; compact inverse regularity retains a strict loss relative to the available gap order.
Norm continuity is proved only after a strict regularity loss. No stronger compactness follows merely from membership plus weak compactness or from an arbitrary bounded stronger realization.

The actual scalar lift family is the full preimage of sourceIsospectralSet, including original periodic spectra and all algebraic multiplicities. Its Hilbert compactness comes from the already verified actual source Birkhoff construction, not a supplied Birkhoff-data parameter.

The original article wrapper retains the entire original isospectral domain and the exact Miura shift. It proves a compact stronger LIFT cover, not compactness of the potential image in its target finite-p norm.
The finite-p Miura image continuity bridge, the uniform endpoint norm bound of Lemma 2.21, source Theorem 2.2(iii), and all five main article theorems remain unproved.
